Thanks for the note and the scorecard, Priyom. Quick technical read: the p95 jump aligns with their rollout of longer context prompts — they moved several routes from 1k->8k tokens and we see degradation at scale on the hosted fleet due to KV cache churn and suboptimal batching for those request shapes.

Proposed short-term engineering triage (owner: Karthik):
- Apply a per-route batching cap and enable prefix cache for the heavy routes (3-5p days to validate).
- Temporarily route the largest jobs to a higher-priority pool (burst capacity) while we stabilize.
- Add a telemetry tag to identify requests >4k tokens for fast filtering.

If we can get engineering committed to the above in 72 hours we should be able to bring p95 down ~30%-40% without changing customer code. Longer-term: consider recommending Dedicated for predictable latency and to remove noisy-neighbor risk.

Commercial note: I do not recommend a full concession yet; propose a goodwill credit tied to a technical milestone (eg p95 < 300ms for three business days). That gives us leverage and avoids setting a precedent.

I'll join the 10:30 PT prep and will loop infra (k8s/serving) if we need deeper instrumentation.

—Rishi
Senior Director, Reliability Engineering
